title: What Is a Cleaning SOP?
excerpt: A cleaning SOP is a controlled set of written instructions that documents how a routine cleaning activity is organized and carried out within a specific facility or program.
content_html:
A cleaning Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) is a controlled set of written instructions for a routine or repetitive cleaning activity. EPA describes SOPs as written instructions that document recurring work so it can be performed consistently.

A cleaning SOP defines scope

The SOP should make clear which area, equipment, surface or activity it covers and which personnel or roles are responsible for the work.

It identifies required resources

Environmental-cleaning SOPs commonly identify the approved supplies, equipment and protective requirements associated with the task. Product-specific details should come from the exact manufacturer documentation and facility program.

It documents the approved work sequence

The SOP records the order in which the facility expects the work to be performed. CDC guidance emphasizes ordered cleaning steps, preparation requirements and close-out steps in environmental-cleaning SOPs.

Safety controls belong in the SOP framework

The document can point to the relevant product labels, SDSs, PPE requirements, training and escalation procedures rather than relying on memory or informal practice.

SOPs need document control

Effective SOP systems use identifiers, revision dates, approvals and current controlled copies so staff can distinguish the active procedure from an obsolete version.

An SOP supports training but does not replace it

Workers still need training and supervision appropriate to the task. The SOP provides the documented reference for the approved method.

References

  1. US EPA — Guidance for Preparing Standard Operating Procedures.
  2. CDC — Environmental Cleaning Programs.
